headline: London Copper Slumps to Five-Month Low on Strong Dollar and AI Fears
summary: Three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange dropped 1.1% to $13,078.50 per tonne, falling for a fifth straight day to its lowest since June, pressured by dollar gains and concerns over AI spending.
why: Copper is an industrial bellwether closely tied to global manufacturing, electrification, and technology infrastructure. Price slides indicate broader macro demand hesitation.
